summary: Synthetic working tree. save() becomes atomic; the rest is a rename, a CLI hook, and assorted files that show each kind of entry the collector writes.

stops.title: save() becomes atomic
stops.summary:
The store now writes a temporary file beside the target and renames it over the old one. A crash during the write leaves the old notes intact instead of a truncated file.

The rename is the only step that changes what readers see.

attention.note: os.replace is atomic on POSIX only when both paths are on the same filesystem. The temporary file is created in the target's directory, so this holds unless the directory is a symlink elsewhere.

notes.title: Same directory
notes.body: mkstemp in target.parent keeps the rename on one filesystem.

notes.title: The swap
notes.body: replace overwrites the old notes in one step.

questions: Should a failed write remove the temporary file?

stops.title: The CLI hook and the rename
stops.summary: format.py replaces render.py and the line format gains the note's date. The CLI wires the new module in.

src/notes/store.py.summary: save() now writes a temporary file in the same directory and renames it over the old one, so a crash cannot leave half a file.

src/notes/format.py.summary: Renamed from render.py. The line format adds the note's date.
